text.p: Germany's national soccer team visited a Holocaust memorial on Tuesday ahead of their historic match against Israel on Wednesday night.
A day before the first game between Israel and a unified Germany, the players and officials went to the Yad Vashem memorial.
"We must make sure to pass on what happened during the Holocaust to the next generations in Germany so that such a thing never, ever happens again," German captain Juergen Klinsmann said.

Israel coach Shlomo Scharf had earlier said on German television that the Holocaust, which claimed the lives of six million Jews, was a thing of the past and that the match between his team and the Germans should not take on historic significance.
"What's past is past," Scharf said in German.
However, his attempt at bridge-building was attacked in Israel and he was berated for his comments.
He subsequently apologised and pointed out that he had lost many of his own relatives during World War Two.
West Germany played Israel in Tel Aviv in 1987, winning 2-0. The countries have never met in Germany.
